Key Finding: On Metro Manila’s EDSA Busway, buses at Main Avenue carried 73 passengers during the southbound evening peak against a stated capacity of 60, including standing passengers.
APA Reference: Ollero, L. J., Vergel, K., & Tiglao, N. C. (2024). A microsimulation model of an exclusive bus lane: The case of EDSA Busway. Philippine Transportation Journal, 7(2), 1–40. https://ncts.upd.edu.ph/tssp/archives/3025

Key Finding: Among bus riders surveyed in metropolitan Seoul, available seats increased the estimated likelihood of boarding the arriving bus, while greater crowding reduced it.
APA Reference: Kim, J.-K., Lee, B., & Oh, S. (2009). Passenger choice models for analysis of impacts of real-time bus information on crowdedness. Transportation Research Record, 2112(1), 119–126. https://www.worldtransitresearch.info/research/8/

Key Finding: After real-time displays were installed at tram stops in The Hague, passengers perceived their waits as 20% shorter, while their reported sense of security was unchanged.
APA Reference: Dziekan, K., & Vermeulen, A. (2006). Psychological effects of and design preferences for real-time information displays. Journal of Public Transportation, 9(1), 1–19. https://doi.org/10.5038/2375-0901.9.1.1

Key Finding: On Android 12 and later, a rider can grant an app approximate location access even when the app requests precise coordinates.
APA Reference: Google. (2026, October 28). Request location access at runtime. Android Developers. https://developer.android.com/develop/sensors-and-location/location/permissions/runtime

Key Finding: A browser can ignore a request for high accuracy, and its geolocation result includes an estimated accuracy radius in metres.
APA Reference: Cáceres, M., & Grant, R. (Eds.). (2026, March 24). Geolocation (W3C Recommendation). World Wide Web Consortium. https://www.w3.org/TR/2026/REC-geolocation-20260324/

Key Finding: In urban field tests with an iPhone 6, average horizontal positioning error ranged from 7 to 13 metres across the conditions tested.
APA Reference: Merry, K., & Bettinger, P. (2019). Smartphone GPS accuracy study in an urban environment. PLOS ONE, 14(7), Article e0219890. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0219890

Key Finding: The Philippine digital connectivity plan reports average household spending of ₱1,069.10 per month on internet in the 2024 national ICT survey.
APA Reference: Department of Information and Communications Technology. (2026). National digital connectivity plan. https://cms-cdn.e.gov.ph/DICT/pdf/LATEST%20PUBLICATION%20NDCP_bda86f60-7dd4-4cf9-be58-c25275508074.pdf

Key Finding: The World Bank reported that a Philippine mobile broadband basket cost 2% of per capita gross national income, about 1.5 times the ASEAN average.
APA Reference: World Bank. (2024). Better internet for all Filipinos: Reforms promoting competition and increasing investment for broadband infrastructure. https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099011824231036851/pdf/P502027179f71d08418678193f2fabcdbec.pdf

Key Finding: In the first half of 2023, 23.8% of families in Leyte excluding Tacloban lived below the poverty threshold, compared with 16.6% in Southern Leyte.
APA Reference: Philippine Statistics Authority Region VIII. (2024, January 18). About 1 in every 4 families in Eastern Visayas is poor. Samar News. https://samarnews.com/news2024/jan/g021.htm

Key Finding: During Tropical Storm Agaton on April 10, 2022, floodwater estimated at 0.5 to 1.2 metres made the VSU Market Road section of the Ormoc–Baybay–Southern Leyte Boundary Road impassable to light vehicles.
APA Reference: National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council. (2022, April 11). SitRep No. 2 for Tropical Storm Agaton (2022). https://adinet.ahacentre.org/assets/uploads/supported_doc/20220411-SitRep_No__2_for_Tropical_Storm_AGATON__2022.pdf

Key Finding: Sogod identifies the mountainous Agas-Agas section of the Pan-Philippine Highway as prone to landslides during heavy rain, particularly during typhoons.
APA Reference: Municipality of Sogod. (2025, March 27). Agas-Agas Bridge. https://www.sogodlgu.gov.ph/tourism/tourist-spot/E4g3nXMcPJd3thiMtPrWPrwRulG0UzVAziKyu8Me/agas-agas-bridge

Key Finding: At the Maasin station in Southern Leyte, the 1991–2020 normals recorded 17 rainy days in December and seven in April, using a threshold of 1 mm per day.
APA Reference: Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration. (n.d.). Climatological normals: Maasin, Southern Leyte, 1991–2020. https://pubfiles.pagasa.dost.gov.ph/pagasaweb/files/cad/CLIMATOLOGICAL%20NORMALS%20(1991-2020)/MAASIN.pdf

Key Finding: Philippine local route-planning guidelines require consultation with commuters, transport groups and the academic community when preparing a local public transport route plan.
APA Reference: Department of the Interior and Local Government. (2018). Memorandum Circular No. 2018-60, § 5.2.4. https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/10/90439

Key Finding: Executive Order No. 202 gives the Philippine Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board authority to prescribe routes, service areas and viable capacities for motorized public land transport.
APA Reference: Creating the Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board, Executive Order No. 202, § 5(a) (1987) (Phil.). https://lawphil.net/executive/execord/eo1987/eo_202_1987.html

Key Finding: In January 2024, an Eastern Visayas transport regulator reported that 3,480 of the region’s 3,692 public utility vehicles had consolidated under the modernization program.
APA Reference: Gabieta, J. A. (2024, January 9). LTFRB-8 announces over 94% consolidation rate in EV. Leyte Samar Daily Express. https://www.leytesamardailynews.com/ltfrb-8-announces-over-94-consolidation-rate-in-ev/

Key Finding: The Philippine Data Privacy Act limits how long personal information may be kept to what its purpose, legal claims, legitimate business needs or the law require.
APA Reference: Data Privacy Act of 2012, Republic Act No. 10173, § 11(e) (2012) (Phil.). https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2012/ra_10173_2012.html

Key Finding: Philippine privacy rules require secure disposal of personal data so that it cannot be processed further, accessed without authorization or disclosed.
APA Reference: National Privacy Commission. (2016). Implementing rules and regulations of the Data Privacy Act of 2012. https://www.pagcor.ph/docs/DPA-Implementing-Rules-and-Regulations.pdf

Key Finding: Under Philippine consent guidelines, a person who gives consent electronically must be able to withdraw it at least as easily as they gave it.
APA Reference: National Privacy Commission. (2023, November 7). Guidelines on consent (NPC Circular No. 2023-04). https://naro.law.upd.edu.ph/issuances/1893

Key Finding: In a dataset of 1.5 million mobile users, four observations of time and cell-tower location uniquely distinguished 95% of individual mobility traces.
APA Reference: de Montjoye, Y.-A., Hidalgo, C. A., Verleysen, M., & Blondel, V. D. (2013). Unique in the crowd: The privacy bounds of human mobility. Scientific Reports, 3, Article 1376. https://doi.org/10.1038/srep01376

Key Finding: Removing identifying information reduces disclosure risk, yet some de-identified records can still be linked back to individuals.
APA Reference: Garfinkel, S. (2015). De-identification of personal information (NISTIR 8053). National Institute of Standards and Technology. https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.IR.8053

Key Finding: Among surveyed OpenStreetMap contributors, the geographic diversity of places mapped by men and women followed different trends over time.
APA Reference: Solomon, G., Sutton, D., Polat Kayali, M., Yuan, X., Gardner, Z., & Basiri, A. (2024). Evaluating geotemporal behaviours of OpenStreetMap contributors. AGILE: GIScience Series, 5, Article 14. https://doi.org/10.5194/agile-giss-5-14-2024
